title: Coral and the Autopsy
premise: Jonah Almeida, the reclusive coroner of Salt Hollow, receives two letters about a drowning victim she never officially logged: one confessing to the death, one promising it was only the first. As she quietly investigates, Jonah realizes the killer is someone with access to her own files—someone from the found family of misfits who orbit her morgue. The trail leads to a decades-old case her late mentor buried, and to the truth that Jonah herself was its unnamed survivor. In the end, Jonah baits the killer with a falsified autopsy report, exposes her mentor's posthumous guilt, and chooses at last to let the town know her real name.
about_author: Ulyana Vasquez is the pen name of a former rural hospice worker who spent eleven years listening to last words in towns too small for traffic lights. She writes mysteries about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Name
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. A John Doe drowns in the tidal flats; that night, twin letters arrive—one confessing to his murder, one promising 'the second will be yours.' Jonah, who has spent years being nobody to everybody, feels seen for the first time and hates it. Emotional beat: dread braided with an unwelcome thrill of recognition.

chapters.title: The Family of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. We meet her circle: deputy Priya Nair, diner owner Marisol, archivist teen Theo, all bound by their exile from elsewhere. Jonah shows no one the letters but begins cross-checking the file—and finds a page missing, cut cleanly, by someone with keys. Emotional beat: paranoia infecting belonging; every kindness now reads as surveillance.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jonah and Theo. Theo, digitizing old records, finds a 1989 drowning ruled accidental—the victim's lungs held the same rare marsh algae as the new body. Jonah recognizes the case number: it's the file her mentor, Coroner Edith Vane, locked away before dying. Emotional beat: the past surfacing like a body refusing to stay down.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. The promised second letter arrives, addressed not to 'Coroner' but to a name Jonah hasn't used since childhood—a name she buried along with her original identity. The writer knows what happened to her at nine years old. She tells Priya nothing. Emotional beat: terror of exposure warring with the ache of finally being known.

chapters.title: Edith's Drawer
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Breaking into her mentor's sealed storage, Jonah finds Edith's private ledger: three drownings across thirty years, each ruled accident, each victim connected to the group home where Jonah once lived. Edith knew. Edith covered. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury—the woman who gave her a family also gave a killer cover.

chapters.title: Everyone Has Keys
chapters.summary: POV: Priya. Priya runs her own quiet inquiry and realizes every person close to Jonah had legitimate access to the files—including herself. When she confronts Jonah gently, Jonah lies, and the first crack splits their friendship. Meanwhile Marisol closes the diner early, shaken. Emotional beat: the found family discovering they were built on shared silence.

chapters.title: The Third Tide
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. A third letter arrives with a tide chart and a time: tomorrow, 4:17 a.m., the flats. Jonah realizes the killer isn't taunting investigators—they're inviting her specifically, staging a reunion of the 1989 survivors. She decides to go alone rather than risk arrest of the wrong friend. Emotional beat: grim resolve; she stops running from her past and starts aiming at it.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah, then Theo. At the flats Jonah finds not a body but a shrine: photographs of the group home children, herself among them, face scratched out except hers. Theo, following secretly, is nearly caught by a figure in a morgue coat. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into clarity—the killer wants Jonah as witness, judge, or final victim.

chapters.title: The Autopsy of Coral Reyes
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Climax. Jonah publishes a falsified report naming 'Coral Reyes'—her birth name—as the next target, forcing the killer to come to the morgue. It's Hollis, the group home's kindly night caretaker, now the town's beloved pharmacy owner, who has been 'finishing' the drowning he caused in 1989 and silencing witnesses Edith protected. Jonah traps him between the cold drawers, recording his confession while he calls her by the name she buried. Emotional beat: confrontation as reclamation.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Aftermath: Hollis is taken, Edith's ledger goes public, and the 1989 victims are reburied under their true names. Jonah stands at the fresh headstones and speaks her own name aloud to the gathered town—Priya, Marisol, Theo beside her. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; invisibility traded, willingly, for belonging.
